newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS TUESDAY MIXED ON UNITS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS TUESDAY MIXED ON UNITS.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar closed on Tuesday easier on the U.S. dollar and pound sterling, pressured by heavy importer buying.
It was, however, quoted firmer against the mark and the rand, tracking overseas market activity.
"There was a bit of heavy (U.S. dollar) buying. We didn't see any significant reaction from the central authority (Reserve Bank)," one dealer said.
He said the market had taken this as a signal that the central Bank was happy with the current levels.

Dealers, however, agreed that trade was on the whole farly subdued, with most of the buying occurring earlier the the day, which resulted in the local currency breaking through the 11.0000 level on the upside against the key U.S. dollar.

The Zimbabwe unit finished Tuesday's interbank session at 11.0100/0200 on the U.S. money, down from 10.9975/11.0075 on Monday and was also quoted weaker on sterling at 18.0400/0600 compared to 17.9455/9730.

It, however, strengthened against the market to 6.5900/6100 from 6.6500/6585 and was at 2.4800/5000 against the rand from 2.4940/4980 the pervious day, cashing in on the rand's losses against the U.S. dollar.
